section: International treaties on chemicals and waste - Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm POPs, Minamata; Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment
subsections: Basel Convention - concern, transboundary waste trade, Ban Amendment
Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years
Minamata Convention - mercury, sources, origin of name
Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification

accepted.s: The Basel Convention primarily addresses which of the following issues?
o: Control of transboundary movement and disposal of hazardous wastes
accepted.x: The Basel Convention controls the transboundary movement of hazardous wastes and their disposal, while promoting environmentally sound management.
accepted.tq: Match the treaty with its precise environmental subject rather than a neighbouring treaty.
accepted.sec: Basel Convention - concern, transboundary waste trade, Ban Amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Basel Convention was adopted in:
accepted.x: The Basel Convention was adopted in Basel, Switzerland, in 1989.
accepted.tq: Use the place-year association to distinguish related environmental treaties.
accepted.sec: Basel Convention - concern, transboundary waste trade, Ban Amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which situation is most directly addressed by the Basel Convention?
o: Emission of HFCs from refrigeration equipment
Physical transfer of hazardous waste across national borders for reprocessing or storage
Accumulation of mercury in marine fish
accepted.x: The Convention addresses the cross-border transfer of hazardous waste, including dumping by richer countries in poorer countries.
accepted.tq: Identify the treaty from the practical environmental situation described.
accepted.sec: Basel Convention - concern, transboundary waste trade, Ban Amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Prior Informed Consent mechanism for implementing the Basel Convention in India operates under which rules?
o: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016
accepted.x: India implements the Basel Convention through the Prior Informed Consent mechanism under the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the exact implementing rules.
accepted.sec: Basel Convention - concern, transboundary waste trade, Ban Amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent developments under the Basel Convention:
1. The plastic waste amendment is operative.
2. Provisions relating to e-waste have been strengthened.
3. The Convention has been confined exclusively to radioactive waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The plastic waste amendment is operative and e-waste provisions have been strengthened. The Convention is not confined to radioactive waste.
accepted.tq: Find the single overbroad statement and retain the two precise developments.
accepted.sec: Basel Convention - concern, transboundary waste trade, Ban Amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ban Amendment to the Basel Convention prohibits exports of hazardous waste from:
o: OECD and European Union countries and Liechtenstein to other countries
Non-OECD countries to the European Union only
All developing countries to OECD countries
All countries to small island developing States
accepted.x: The Ban Amendment prohibits exports of hazardous waste from OECD/EU countries and Liechtenstein to other countries.
accepted.tq: Check the exact membership and direction of the prohibition.
accepted.sec: Basel Convention - concern, transboundary waste trade, Ban Amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Basel Convention Ban Amendment came into force on:
accepted.x: The Ban Amendment entered into force on 5 December 2019.
accepted.tq: Separate the amendment’s effective date from the parent convention’s adoption date.
accepted.sec: Basel Convention - concern, transboundary waste trade, Ban Amendment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kigali Amendment was adopted at:
accepted.x: The Kigali Amendment was adopted in Kigali, Rwanda, in 2016.
accepted.tq: Use place-year pairing to distinguish the four chemical and waste agreements.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kigali Amendment entered into force on:
accepted.x: The Kigali Amendment entered into force on 1 January 2019.
accepted.tq: Test the commencement year independently of the adoption year.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which gases are specifically targeted for phase-down under the Kigali Amendment?
accepted.x: The Kigali Amendment is legally binding and phases down hydrofluorocarbons, or HFCs.
accepted.tq: Use exact gas identification rather than confusing ozone-depleting substances with high-GWP gases.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about HFCs:
1. They replaced ozone-depleting substances in air-conditioners and refrigerators.
2. They do not deplete ozone.
3. They have very high global warming potential.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: HFCs replaced ODS in cooling equipment, do not deplete ozone, and possess high global warming potential.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between ozone depletion and global warming potential.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kigali Amendment seeks to reduce HFC use by approximately what percentage by the late 2040s?
accepted.x: The overall target is an 80–85% phase-down of HFC use by the late 2040s.
accepted.tq: Identify the broad target range without reversing phase-down and phase-out terminology.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Developed countries are required to achieve an 85% reduction in HFCs by:
accepted.x: Developed countries are scheduled to reach an 85% reduction by 2036.
accepted.tq: Match the final-cut percentage with the correct group and year.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India belongs to which Kigali Amendment group, and what are its baseline and freeze years?
accepted.x: India belongs to Group 2, along with Gulf States, Iran, Iraq and Pakistan. Its baseline is 2024–26 and its freeze year is 2028.
accepted.tq: Split the options by group first, then verify the associated baseline and freeze years.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following countries or groups is associated with Developing Group 1 under the Kigali Amendment?
o: China and other countries in the 2020–22 baseline group
accepted.x: Developing Group 1 includes China and has a 2020–22 baseline, a 2024 freeze and an 80% final cut by 2045.
accepted.tq: Use group membership as the sure pair before checking the dates.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s Kigali Amendment schedule provides for HFC reductions of 10%, 20% and 30% in which years respectively?
accepted.x: India’s intermediate reduction steps are 10% by 2032, 20% by 2037 and 30% by 2042.
accepted.tq: Preserve the chronological sequence when matching percentages to years.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s final HFC reduction target under the Kigali Amendment is:
accepted.x: India, as a member of Group 2, is to achieve an 85% final cut by 2047.
accepted.tq: Distinguish India’s Group 2 endpoint from the developed-country endpoint.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Full implementation of the Kigali Amendment could avoid approximately how much warming by 2100?
accepted.x: Full implementation of the Kigali Amendment could avoid up to 0.5°C of warming by 2100.
accepted.tq: Reject the misplaced decimal by identifying the precise quantitative estimate.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding India’s recent HFC regulatory direction is correct?
o: All HFC production must cease immediately after 31 December 2027.
The direction applies only to private authorities and not to government authorities.
No environmental clearance may be granted for new or additional HFC production after 31 December 2027.
Environmental clearance is required only for HFC imports after 31 December 2027.
accepted.x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change directed Central and State authorities to stop granting environmental clearances for new or additional HFC production after 31 December 2027.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a restriction on new clearances from a complete production ban.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 37th Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol focused particularly on:
o: Banning international trade in endangered species
accepted.x: MOP37 of the Montreal Protocol focused on implementing the Kigali Amendment.
accepted.tq: Match the meeting with the agreement or amendment it addressed.
accepted.sec: Kigali Amendment - HFC uses, gases targeted, India's group and years  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Minamata Convention is primarily concerned with protection from:
o: Emission of HFCs from cooling appliances
Man-made emissions of mercury and mercury compounds
accepted.x: The Minamata Convention protects human health and the environment from anthropogenic emissions of mercury and mercury compounds across the mercury lifecycle.
accepted.tq: Match the treaty with its defining pollutant.
accepted.sec: Minamata Convention - mercury, sources, origin of name  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Minamata Convention:
1. It was adopted in 2013.
2. It entered into force in 2017.
3. It has more than 140 Parties.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Minamata Convention was adopted in 2013, entered into force in 2017 and has more than 140 Parties.
accepted.tq: Verify each date and membership figure independently before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Minamata Convention - mercury, sources, origin of name  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a major source of mercury emissions?
o: Solar photovoltaic panels in normal operation
accepted.x: Major sources include coal-fired power plants, artisanal and small-scale gold mining, industrial processes and waste. Solar photovoltaic panels in normal operation are not listed as a major source.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the recognised source group rather than choosing by pollutant association alone.
accepted.sec: Minamata Convention - mercury, sources, origin of name  [other exams]

accepted.s: The name ‘Minamata’ is associated with:
o: A major oil spill in the Pacific Ocean
A mercury-poisoning episode caused by contaminated factory wastewater in Japan
accepted.x: The Convention is named after Minamata, Japan, where factory wastewater contaminated local fish with mercury and poisoned people in the 1950s. The illness became known as Minamata disease.
accepted.tq: Infer the treaty from the historical pollution episode behind its name.
accepted.sec: Minamata Convention - mercury, sources, origin of name  [other exams]

accepted.s: The latest decision mentioned in relation to the Minamata Convention seeks to phase out dental amalgam by:
accepted.x: The latest decision seeks to phase out dental amalgam by 2034.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific phase-out deadline rather than the Convention’s entry-into-force year.
accepted.sec: Minamata Convention - mercury, sources, origin of name  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Stockholm Convention was adopted in 2001 and entered into force in:
accepted.x: The Stockholm Convention was adopted in 2001 and entered into force in 2004.
accepted.tq: Separate adoption and entry-into-force years in a treaty timeline.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: Persistent Organic Pollutants are characterised by which combination of properties?
o: Toxicity, long persistence, bioaccumulation and long-distance transport
Radioactivity, water solubility and immediate evaporation
High biodegradability, low toxicity and limited mobility
Short persistence, rapid breakdown and local movement only
accepted.x: POPs are toxic chemicals that persist for long periods, build up in living tissue and travel long distances.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete defining property cluster.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Stockholm Convention initially covered how many POPs, commonly called the ‘dirty dozen’?
accepted.x: The Convention initially covered 12 POPs, popularly known as the ‘dirty dozen’.
accepted.tq: Test the standard numerical association of the initial list.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the initial ‘dirty dozen’ POPs?
accepted.x: DDT, PCBs, dioxins and furans were among the initial 12 POPs. Chlorpyrifos was added to Annex A in 2025, not included in the initial dirty dozen.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original list from later additions.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the remaining members of the initial ‘dirty dozen’ besides DDT, PCBs, dioxins and furans?
o: Aldrin, chlordane, dieldrin, endrin, heptachlor, hexachlorobenzene, mirex and toxaphene
Chlorpyrifos, long-chain PFCAs, UV-328 and dental amalgam
Pentachlorobenzene, chlordecone, chlorpyrifos and PFCAs only
accepted.x: The other eight initial POPs were aldrin, chlordane, dieldrin, endrin, heptachlor, hexachlorobenzene, mirex and toxaphene.
accepted.tq: Use elimination to identify the complete original chemical list rather than later additions.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Annex)
a. Annex A
b. Annex B
c. Annex C
List-II (Meaning)
i. Unintentional by-products
ii. Elimination
iii. Restriction
accepted.x: Annex A concerns elimination, Annex B concerns restriction and Annex C concerns unintentional by-products.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes that reverse the annex meanings.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched under the Stockholm Convention?
o: Annex A — DDT limited use for malaria control
Annex B — dioxins and furans as unintentional by-products
Annex B — DDT restricted, including limited use for malaria control
accepted.x: DDT is listed in Annex B for restriction, with limited use permitted for malaria control. Aldrin and dieldrin are associated with Annex A, while dioxins and furans are Annex C examples.
accepted.tq: Check whether the example is paired with the correct annex function.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following chemicals was added to Annex A of the Stockholm Convention in 2025?
accepted.x: Chlorpyrifos was among the chemicals added to Annex A in 2025. It is a neurotoxic insecticide.
accepted.tq: Distinguish recent additions from chemicals already present in the initial list.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2025 additions to Annex A:
1. Long-chain PFCAs are described as ‘forever chemicals’ and belong to the PFAS family.
2. Medium-chain chlorinated paraffins are used in plastics.
3. Chlorpyrifos is a neurotoxic insecticide.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct descriptions of the 2025 Annex A additions.
accepted.tq: Retain all three precise descriptions while rejecting no supported statement.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: The current number of chemicals listed under the Stockholm Convention, as stated, is:
accepted.x: The Convention is stated to list 34 chemicals, although some reference sources continue to mention lower figures.
accepted.tq: Prefer the specified current figure over the original list size or outdated count.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which body assesses candidate chemicals for possible listing as Persistent Organic Pollutants under the Stockholm Convention?
accepted.x: The POPs Review Committee, or POPRC, assesses candidate chemicals for possible listing.
accepted.tq: Identify the specialised reviewing body rather than a neighbouring international institution.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: India ratified the Stockholm Convention in:
accepted.x: India ratified the Stockholm Convention in 2006.
accepted.tq: Distinguish India’s ratification year from the Convention’s adoption and entry-into-force years.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s: In 2020, India ratified seven additional POPs, including which of the following?
o: Chlorpyrifos, PFCAs, paraffins, HFCs and mercury
DDT, PCBs, dioxins, furans and aldrin only
HFCs, mercury, methane, sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides
Chlordecone, hexabromobiphenyl, pentachlorobenzene, hexabromocyclododecane and hexachlorobutadiene
accepted.x: The seven additional POPs ratified by India in 2020 included chlordecone, hexabromobiphenyl, pentachlorobenzene, hexabromocyclododecane and hexachlorobutadiene.
accepted.tq: Recognise the exact chemical cluster and reject pollutants belonging to other treaties.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Adoption of the Stockholm Convention
B. India’s ratification of the Stockholm Convention
C. Entry into force of the Stockholm Convention
D. India’s ratification of seven additional POPs
accepted.x: The Stockholm Convention was adopted in 2001, entered into force in 2004, India ratified it in 2006, and India ratified seven additional POPs in 2020.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate dates.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Convention - initial POPs, new chemicals, India's ratification  [other exams]
